gen_risks.description: Concentrated banking system and conservative risk appetite among Mexican financial institutions may limit PFIs' willingness to extend long-term green loans to SMEs, constraining sub-loan uptake.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted technical assistance and training to PFI teams under Component 2, blend concessional CCEFCF funding to lower capital costs, and establish clear eligibility guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: a concentrated banking system with conservative risk appetite, weak competition, short-term funding structures... constrain financial access.

gen_risks.description: SMEs and mid-caps lack internal technical capacity to measure emissions, formulate Sustainability Plans, and establish MRV systems, threatening sub-loan eligibility and target verification.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Component 2 technical assistance to support firms in preparing Sustainability Plans, conducting feasibility assessments, and building internal MRV capacities.
gen_risks.evidence: Most Mexican firms lack the capacity to measure emissions, implement energy-use, generation or management systems, and comply with reporting frameworks

gen_risks.description: Superficial or unchallenging sustainability performance targets set in firm Sustainability Plans could lead to greenwashing and reputational damage for the project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate independent ex-ante validation of Sustainability Plans and ex-post verification of KPI performance by qualified third-party validation entities.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to, respectively, ex-ante validation and ex-post verification

gen_risks.description: Providing local currency sub-loans while borrowing foreign currency funds exposes NAFIN to foreign exchange volatility risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require NAFIN to manage foreign exchange risk on its balance sheet utilizing Mexico's currency swap market and restrict USD lending to firms with clear natural export hedges.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market.

gen_risks.description: Subprojects financed through PFIs or direct lending may generate adverse environmental and social impacts if E&S risk management standards are inadequately applied.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce NAFIN's ESMS due diligence, apply a strict Exclusion List excluding high E&S risk activities, and conduct World Bank sample reviews and biannual performance reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social (E&S) risk is assessed as Substantial, considering the nature of the financial instruments to be used

gen_risks.description: NAFIN's lack of direct experience executing World Bank procurement selection processes could lead to implementation delays for Component 2 contracts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a dedicated internal procurement specialist to the project team and deliver hands-on training and implementation support from the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes.

gen_risks.description: Reliance on NAFIN's legacy information systems requiring manual data consolidation creates risk of operational errors and financial reporting delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear FM workflows and detailed PFI reporting rules in the Project Operations Manual, backed by supervisory reviews and targeted internal and external audits.
gen_risks.evidence: efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation, the need to consistently apply financial intermediary–specific controls

gen_risks.description: Severe weather events, drought, and extreme heatwaves could disrupt beneficiary enterprise operations, leading to liquidity shortages and sub-loan defaults.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target project investments toward climate resilience, energy efficiency, and water-saving technologies, while integrating climate risk assessments into subproject appraisal.
gen_risks.evidence: BEs could be slightly impacted by heat‑related productivity losses, water scarcity or energy‑supply disruptions.

gen_risks.description: High upfront costs, complex paperwork, and expensive MRV requirements could deter prospective SME borrowers from applying for project-supported loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize ESMAP grant funds to cover ex-ante validation and verification costs during initial rollout and provide standardized templates to minimize administrative burden.
gen_risks.evidence: high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity to structure, appraise and monitor investments.

gen_risks.description: Persistent structural and social barriers faced by female-led businesses in Mexico could prevent women entrepreneurs from accessing project credit lines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute a targeted gender-focused communication campaign, apply transparent access criteria for women-inclusive enterprises, and track progress via dedicated gender indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing: only 46 percent have ever sought credit compared to 50 percent of firms nationally

gen_risks.description: Delays in preparing and formally adopting the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework could push back project effectiveness and initial disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage GFPP preparation grant resources to complete and finalize the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework prior to loan effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Additional Conditions of Effectiveness consist of... the Borrower has adopted the Project Operations Manual... and prepared and adopted the Sustainable Finance Framework

gen_risks.description: Credit defaults by direct mid-cap borrowers or second-tier participating financial institutions could cause financial losses for NAFIN.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce rigorous financial soundness criteria for PFIs and BEs, set single-borrower exposure limits, and include credit risk margins in on-lending interest rates.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations

gen_risks.description: Increasing global and domestic sustainability disclosure mandates may result in forward-exclusion of Mexican SME suppliers from global value chains if adoption of green practices is delayed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate that at least 50 percent of GHG reductions under SLLs and 40 percent of GL proceeds target clean energy and energy efficiency investments, supporting rapid compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: Global and domestic regulatory and disclosure requirements... are prompting large anchor companies to assess the environmental performance of their suppliers

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
